task.instruction: Compare the prices of the latest models of MacBook Air available on Apple's website.

final_answer:
Here's the pricing for the latest MacBook Air models on Apple's website (apple.com, U.S. store):

**MacBook Air 13-inch (M5)** — from **$1,299** (or $108.25/mo. for 12 months; lease from $24.99/mo. for 36 months with Apple Upgrade). Standard config: M5 with 10-core CPU / 8-core GPU, 16GB unified memory, 512GB SSD, 13.6-inch Liquid Retina display, up to 18 hours battery life.

**MacBook Air 15-inch (M5)** — from **$1,499** (or $124.91/mo. for 12 months; lease from $28.99/mo. for 36 months). Same M5 chip, memory and storage starting points, but a larger 15.3-inch Liquid Retina display and a 10-core GPU as standard.

**Key takeaway:** the 15-inch model costs exactly **$200 more** than the 13-inch. For that premium you get a bigger screen, a slightly better standard GPU (10-core vs. 8-core), and a four-speaker sound system — the chip, memory (16GB–32GB), storage (512GB–4TB), and battery life (up to 18 hrs) are otherwise the same across both sizes. Both come in Sky Blue, Silver, Starlight, and Midnight.

For reference, the comparison page also lists the MacBook Neo (A18 Pro) at $699, but that's a separate, lower-tier model rather than a MacBook Air. Note these are U.S. prices — Apple's site detected a Malaysia region, so local pricing in MYR may differ if you shop the Malaysian storefront.

judge.rationale: Final answer matches Apple compare page evidence showing MacBook Air 13-in. M5 from $1299 and 15-in. M5 from $1499, a $200 difference.
